question: Who invented the small pox vaccine?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Edward Jenner**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Edward Jenner** is credited with the invention of the smallpox vaccine.
 
• Jenner, an English physician and scientist, developed the first successful vaccine in 1796.
 
• He used material from cowpox pustules to create immunity to smallpox, a method that proved to be effective.
 
• This groundbreaking work laid the foundation for modern immunology and vaccination practices.
 
• Smallpox was declared eradicated in 1980, thanks to the widespread use of the vaccine initiated by Jenner's discovery.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Edward Jenner** was born on 17 May 1749 and died on 26 January 1823.
 
• He is often referred to as the "father of immunology."
 
• Jenner's method of vaccination was initially met with skepticism but eventually gained acceptance and led to the development of other vaccines.
 
• The World Health Organization (WHO) has recognized Jenner's contribution as a milestone in the field of medicine.
 
• Jenner's work has saved countless lives and continues to influence public health policies worldwide.
